name: GS12572 VPA-3 Sustainable Paddy Cultivation Initiative in India
description: This VPA intends to help farmers adopt new improved irrigation practice in paddy in India. Improved irrigation practices include Alternate wetting and drying (AWD) to reduce methane emission from paddy field. AWD is a proven method to reduce CH4 emission by as much as 48% compared to continuously flooded conditions where high rates of CH4 are emitted by the lands due to the anaerobic decomposition of the organic matter. The overarching goal of the project activities is to implement sustainable irrigation management techniques that reduce methane emission and advance the socioeconomic situation of the project region. The VPA aims to reduce estimated GHG emission (tCO2e) of 52,821 tCO2e / year.

name: Developing sustainable rice value chains for   smallholder farmers in Dong Thap from 2022 –  2035
description:
This project introduces Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) as a climate-smart water management practice in rice farming in Dong Thap Province, a major rice-producing area of the Mekong Delta. The project aims to reduce methane emissions from rice cultivation, save irrigation water, and support sustainable rice production. It is being implemented by Rikolto in Vietnam acting on behalf of Livelihoods Carbon Fund (LCF3).
The core technical intervention of the project is the application of AWD, a water-saving irrigation technique that reduces methane emissions in rice cultivation. Instead of keeping rice paddies continuously flooded, AWD involves allowing the field to dry intermittently, typically until the water level drops 15 cm below the soil surface, at which point irrigation is resumed with a shallow flood of 2–5 cm. This practice reduces the anaerobic conditions in the soil that are responsible for methane generation, without negatively affecting rice yields. 
To support this method, the project installs PVC monitoring tubes (commonly known as pani-pipes) in farmers’ fields. These tools allow farmers to visually monitor the water level in the soil and make informed irrigation decisions, making AWD both accessible and easy to implement.
In addition to water management, the project promotes improved straw and fertilizer practices. Rather than incorporating straw into the soil, which significantly contributes to methane emissions, farmers are encouraged to remove, compost, or repurpose straw for other uses such as mushroom cultivation. Fertilizer use is also optimized to improve nitrogen efficiency and reduce emissions of nitrous oxide (N₂O), another potent greenhouse gas.

name: GHG Emissions Reduction & Sequestration - Afforestation/Reforestation - Future Radici (Lanuvio-Roma-Lazio)
description:
The Real Case VPA Future Radici, Lanuvio represents a pivotal and strategic initiative within the broader framework of the Programme of Activities (PoA) Future Radici. Located in the municipality of Lanuvio (Rome), the project spans a total area of 403.9 hectares across three agricultural estates: Solonio, Presciano, and Campoleone. These lands are owned by Leone Alato SpA. The project envisions the planting of approximately 422,000 trees, with the goal of transforming these agricultural lands into thriving, biodiverse forest ecosystems.
The primary objective of the Real Case of Lanuvio is to establish native and ecologically rich forest environments through a combination of afforestation and agroforestry practices. These practices are carefully tailored to the pedoclimatic and ecological characteristics of each site, ensuring that the interventions enhance biodiversity, support complex habitats, and maximize long-term carbon sequestration. The forest models adopted in this project are non-extractive, the harvesting of timber or biomass is explicitly excluded. This commitment extends for a minimum duration of 60 years.
To quantify the carbon absorption, the project will rely on methodologies recommended by the IPCC (Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change). These methods will be calibrated using national and regional data. The goal is to produce credits that are measurable, verifiable, and directly linked to positive outcomes in both biodiversity and social impact.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: GHG Emissions Reduction & Sequestration - Afforestation/Reforestation - Future Radici
description: The Future Radici Programme of Activities (PoA) represents a voluntary, long-term climate and biodiversity initiative developed and managed by Leone Alato SpA, the Coordinating and Managing Entity (CME). It has been conceived as an afforestation and reforestation (A/R) programme to address the interlinked crises of climate change, biodiversity degradation, and ecosystem loss. By planting native, long-cycle, non-invasive trees within the Leone Alato perimeter (Italy end Romania), the overarching aim is to contribute substantively to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), with a principal focus on SDG 13 (Climate Action) through the biological removal and long-term storage of atmospheric carbon dioxide via A/R practices. In doing so, the PoA also contributes to SDG 15 (Life on Land) through the restoration of degraded ecosystems and the strengthening of biodiversity, as well as to SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production) by reducing synthetic fertilizers and pesticides, and SDG 5 (Gender Equality) by generating inclusive and equitable socioeconomic opportunities within local communities.

name: MuLaKiLa
description: The MuLaKiLa project is a long-term (32 years) community-based landscape restoration and climate resilience initiative in Rwanda’s western province, spanning Ngororero and Rutsiro districts. As part of the voluntary carbon market, it is projected to sequester 5.4 million tons of CO₂e, with 4.356 million tons of CO₂e accounted for after buffer deduction. The project will restore 21,000 hectares of degraded smallholder land through agroforestry systems, woodlots, and Sustainable Agriculture Land Management (SALM) practices. It will benefit around 160,000 farmers by creating green jobs, improving livelihoods, and addressing climate challenges such as soil erosion, land degradation, and biodiversity loss. Core interventions include planting over 6 million trees, community mobilization, capacity building, and the establishment of innovative nature-based financial mechanisms.

name: FS BECCS Project
description:
The FS BECCS project, proposed under the Gold Standard for Global Goals (GS4GG), reflects FS – Fueling Sustainability’s ambition to lead Brazil’s energy transition with innovation, technical excellence, and private investment. Founded in 2017, FS is the third-largest ethanol producer in the country, operating modern plants in Mato Grosso.

At its Lucas do Rio Verde facility, FS will capture biogenic CO₂ from corn ethanol fermentation. The stream, with about 98% purity, will be compressed, dehydrated, and injected into deep geological formations of the Parecis Basin for secure, long-term storage. As this CO₂ originates from the atmosphere via photosynthesis, its storage delivers net carbon removals.

Project development followed four phases: Phase 1 (2019–2020) confirmed storage potential through feasibility studies and 2D seismic data. Phase 2 (2020–2022) added a 3D seismic survey and design of capture and compression systems. Phase 3 (2022–2024) drilled a stratigraphic well, collected geological data, and began equipment procurement. Phase 4 (2024–2026), now underway, includes injectivity tests, well conversion, monitoring infrastructure, and capture system construction. Commercial operations are expected in 2025, with carbon injection June 2026.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
